itinerary.title: Arrival at Chopta | Journey Through the Himalayas
itinerary.description: Your Himalayan adventure begins with your journey towards Chopta. As you travel through the beautiful landscapes of Uttarakhand, enjoy changing views of rivers, valleys, forests and mountain roads. On arrival in Chopta, check in to your campsite or accommodation and take some time to relax. The fresh mountain air and peaceful surroundings provide the perfect introduction to the Himalayas. In the evening, enjoy dinner, interact with fellow travelers and prepare for the next day's trek.

itinerary.title: Chopta to Tungnath and Chandrashila Summit | Trek Day
itinerary.description: Wake up early and get ready for the most exciting day of the trip. After breakfast, begin your trek from Chopta towards Tungnath Temple. The trail gradually takes you through beautiful Himalayan landscapes and offers incredible views of the surrounding mountains. Reach Tungnath Temple and spend some time exploring this sacred Himalayan destination. After visiting Tungnath, continue towards the Chandrashila Summit. The final section of the trek can be steep, but reaching the summit is a rewarding experience. From Chandrashila, enjoy panoramic views of the Himalayan ranges, subject to weather and visibility. After spending time at the summit, begin your descent back towards Chopta. In the evening, relax at your accommodation and enjoy dinner.

itinerary.title: Chopta to Departure Point | Memories for a Lifetime
itinerary.description: Wake up to another beautiful Himalayan morning. After breakfast, check out from your accommodation and begin your return journey with unforgettable memories of Chopta, Tungnath and Chandrashila. The trip concludes with memories of mountain views, peaceful landscapes, new friendships and an incredible trekking experience. treks.overview:
Experience the beauty of the Garhwal Himalayas with the Chopta Tungnath Chandrashila Trek, one of Uttarakhand's most popular Himalayan adventures.

From the beautiful alpine meadows of Chopta to the sacred Tungnath Temple and the breathtaking Chandrashila Summit, this journey offers a perfect combination of adventure, spirituality, nature and Himalayan views.

The trek takes you through scenic mountain roads, dense forests and high-altitude trails. Tungnath, one of the sacred Panch Kedar temples, is an important spiritual destination, while Chandrashila offers spectacular panoramic views of the surrounding Himalayan peaks.

Whether you are a first-time trekker, a nature lover or an adventure enthusiast, the Chopta Tungnath Chandrashila Trek promises an unforgettable Himalayan experience.

itinerary.title: Manali to Jobra and Trek to Chika
itinerary.description: Drive: Manali – Jobra Trek: Jobra – Chika Approx. Trek Distance: 3 km Trek Duration: 1.5–2.5 hours Your Hampta Pass adventure begins from Manali. After meeting the trek team and completing the necessary formalities, you drive towards Jobra, the roadhead for the trek. The route passes through beautiful mountain scenery as you leave the busy surroundings of Manali behind. From Jobra, the trek begins with a relatively easy walk towards Chika. The trail passes through green landscapes and mountain vegetation before reaching the campsite. After reaching Chika, settle into your tent, enjoy a warm meal and prepare for the next day's longer walk. Overnight stay: Chika campsite.

itinerary.title: Chika to Balu Ka Ghera
itinerary.description: Trek Duration: 5–6 hours After breakfast, begin the trek towards Balu Ka Ghera. The trail gradually moves through open valleys, meadows and rocky sections. Depending on the season, the landscape can be filled with wildflowers and flowing mountain streams. You will cross several small water channels, and the flow of streams can vary considerably with weather conditions. As you gain altitude, the landscape becomes more rugged and the mountains appear closer. Eventually, you reach Balu Ka Ghera, a scenic campsite surrounded by high Himalayan terrain. The evening is spent resting and preparing for the most demanding day of the trek. Overnight stay: Balu Ka Ghera campsite.

itinerary.title: Balu Ka Ghera to Hampta Pass to Shea Goru
itinerary.description: Trek Duration: 8–10 hours Maximum Altitude: Approx. 14,000 ft This is the most challenging and rewarding day of the Hampta Pass Trek. Start early after breakfast because the trail to the pass involves a significant climb. The route becomes steeper and more rugged as you approach the pass. The terrain can include loose rocks, boulders, snow patches and narrow sections depending on the season. After reaching Hampta Pass, take time to appreciate the extraordinary landscape. Behind you lies the greener Kullu side, while ahead is the dry and dramatic Lahaul region. After spending some time at the pass, begin the descent towards Shea Goru. The descent can be tiring after the summit climb, so maintain a controlled pace and follow the instructions of your trek leader. Overnight stay: Shea Goru campsite.

itinerary.title: Shea Goru to Chhatru and Optional Chandratal Excursion
itinerary.description: Trek: Shea Goru – Chhatru Approx. Trek Distance: 6–7 km Drive: Chhatru – Chandratal – Chhatru The day begins with a descent towards Chhatru. The surroundings are now completely different from the green Kullu Valley. The landscape around Lahaul is dry, rocky and dramatic, with towering mountains surrounding the valley. After reaching Chhatru, the group may proceed towards Chandratal Lake, depending on road accessibility, weather, local administration and operational conditions. Chandratal is famous for its crescent-like shape and striking blue waters. Spend some time around the lake while following all local environmental guidelines. Return to Chhatru for the night. Important: Chandratal access can be affected by weather, road conditions, local restrictions and other factors. The excursion should never be considered guaranteed.

itinerary.title: Chhatru to Manali
itinerary.description: Drive Distance: Approx. 60–70 km Drive Duration: Approx. 4–6 hours End Point: Manali After breakfast, begin the drive back towards Manali. The journey takes you through the spectacular landscapes of Lahaul before gradually returning to the greener surroundings near Manali. Your Hampta Pass Trek concludes after reaching Manali. We recommend keeping your onward travel flexible because mountain roads can be affected by weather, traffic, road repair work, landslides or other unforeseen circumstances. Best Time for Hampta Pass Trek The main trekking season for Hampta Pass generally falls between June and September. June Early-season conditions can bring snow to higher sections of the trail. The landscape begins transforming from spring greenery to the summer trekking season. July The valleys become greener and streams may have stronger water flow. Weather can be unpredictable, so proper rain protection is important. August August can offer lush landscapes and beautiful greenery on the Kullu side. However, rainfall and stream conditions can make some sections more challenging. September The weather generally starts becoming clearer, and the landscape begins moving towards the autumn season. Conditions can still change quickly at high altitude. Note: Himalayan weather is unpredictable. Trek dates and route accessibility can change according to local weather and government or forest department regulations. Hampta Pass Trek Difficulty Difficulty Level: Moderate Hampta Pass is often chosen by first-time trekkers because the overall trekking distance is manageable compared with many longer Himalayan routes. However, it is still a high-altitude trek and should not be treated as an easy walk. The main challenges include: * Significant altitude gain * Long summit day * Steep ascents and descents * Rocky and uneven terrain * River and stream crossings * Cold temperatures at higher camps * Possible snow on the upper trail * Weather changes * Limited access to medical facilities A good level of cardiovascular fitness, regular walking practice and basic strength training can make the trek much more comfortable. Who Can Do the Hampta Pass Trek? Hampta Pass can be suitable for beginners with good physical preparation. You should be comfortable walking approximately 5–8 km on consecutive trekking days, including uphill and downhill sections. Before joining the trek, participants should be capable of: * Walking continuously for several hours * Managing moderate uphill climbs * Walking on uneven mountain trails * Carrying a daypack * Handling cold and changing weather * Following trek leader instructions If you have any existing medical concern or have been advised by a doctor to avoid strenuous or high-altitude activity, consult a qualified medical professional before booking. Hampta Pass Trek Fitness Preparation Start preparing at least 4–6 weeks before the trek. Walking / Cardio Begin with regular brisk walking, jogging, cycling or stair climbing. Gradually increase your walking duration and include uphill routes whenever possible. Strength Training Focus on: * Squats * Lunges * Step-ups * Calf raises * Core exercises Endurance Try to build towards a sustained workout of approximately 45–60 minutes. The goal is not speed. The goal is to develop the stamina needed for long mountain days. Hampta Pass Trek Packing List Clothing * Quick-dry trekking T-shirts * Trekking trousers * Thermal innerwear * Fleece jacket * Warm down/synthetic jacket * Waterproof jacket * Waterproof trekking pants * Woollen cap * Sun cap * Gloves * Warm socks * Extra innerwear Footwear * Good-quality trekking shoes with proper grip * Camp sandals/slippers * Extra shoelaces Backpack * 40–60 litre trekking backpack * Small daypack * Rain cover * Waterproof packing bags Personal Essentials * Sunglasses * Sunscreen * Lip balm * Personal medicines * Basic toiletries * Water bottles * Headlamp * Power bank * Personal identification document * Small towel * Hand sanitiser * Waste bags Optional * Trekking poles * Camera * Energy bars * Personal hydration/electrolyte solution Avoid carrying unnecessary luggage. A lighter backpack makes long trekking days considerably easier.

faqs.question: Is Hampta Pass Trek suitable for beginners?
faqs.answer: Yes. Hampta Pass can be a good introduction to moderate Himalayan trekking for beginners who are physically prepared. The trek still involves altitude, steep sections, river crossings and a demanding summit day, so preparation is important.

faqs.question: How difficult is Hampta Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: Hampta Pass is generally classified as a moderate trek. The summit day is the most demanding part because of the altitude gain, steep climb and long trekking hours.

faqs.question: What is the maximum altitude of Hampta Pass?
faqs.answer: Hampta Pass is approximately 14,000 ft above sea level, with exact figures varying slightly between sources and route conditions.

faqs.question: How many days are required for Hampta Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: A typical organised itinerary takes around 5 days, including the approach from Manali and return. Some operators may use different itinerary structures or add buffer days.

faqs.question: What is the best month for Hampta Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: The main trekking window is generally from June to September, subject to weather and local conditions.

faqs.question: Is Hampta Pass Trek safe?
faqs.answer: Hampta Pass can be undertaken safely with proper preparation, experienced guidance and responsible trekking practices. However, no Himalayan trek is completely risk-free.

faqs.question: Can children join the trek?
faqs.answer: Children should only participate if they meet the trek operator's age, fitness and safety requirements. Parents or guardians should assess the child's ability to manage long mountain walks and altitude.

faqs.question: Can senior citizens join Hampta Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: Age alone should not determine suitability. However, the physical demands and altitude make medical and fitness assessment particularly important for older participants.

faqs.question: Is Chandratal included in Hampta Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: Chandratal is included in some itineraries and offered as an excursion, but access depends on road conditions, weather, local restrictions and the operational itinerary. It should not be assumed to be guaranteed.

faqs.question: Will there be snow on Hampta Pass?
faqs.answer: Snow conditions depend on the time of year and the year's weather. Early-season departures are more likely to encounter snow at higher elevations, but conditions vary every season.

faqs.question: What type of accommodation is provided?
faqs.answer: The trek generally uses camping accommodation. Facilities are basic and intended for rest and shelter in a mountain environment.

faqs.question: Do I need trekking shoes?
faqs.answer: Yes. Proper trekking shoes with good grip are strongly recommended because the trail includes rocky, uneven and potentially wet sections.

faqs.question: Is there mobile network during the trek?
faqs.answer: Mobile connectivity can be intermittent or unavailable across several sections of the route. Do not rely on your phone as your only means of communication.

faqs.question: Can I charge my phone during the trek?
faqs.answer: Charging facilities may be limited or unavailable at campsites. Carry a fully charged power bank.

faqs.question: Can I rent trekking equipment?
faqs.answer: Equipment rental may be available depending on the package and operational arrangements. Confirm availability with KRAD Global before departure.

faqs.question: What should I carry for Hampta Pass?
faqs.answer: Carry suitable trekking shoes, warm layers, rain protection, personal medication, sunscreen, sunglasses, a headlamp, water bottles, personal toiletries and other essentials mentioned in the packing list.

faqs.question: How fit should I be for Hampta Pass?
faqs.answer: You should be able to walk several kilometres for multiple consecutive days and manage uphill and downhill sections comfortably. Regular cardio and strength training before the trek is recommended.

itinerary.title: Reach Barshaini and Trek to Kheerganga
itinerary.description: Route: Barshaini → Nakthan → Rudranag → Kheerganga → Return/overnight stay in lower valley Trek Time: Around 5–6 hours depending on pace and trail conditions Start early from Barshaini, the roadhead and standard base for the Kheerganga trek. Before beginning the hike, make sure you have enough water, snacks, rain protection and essential trekking equipment. The trail initially follows the Parvati Valley and crosses the Parvati River. From the Barshaini area, the popular route heads towards Nakthan Village. Barshaini to Nakthan Village Nakthan is one of the key settlements on the traditional Kheerganga route. The trail passes through mountain homes, forest sections and open stretches with views towards the surrounding valley. This section can feel relatively exposed in sunny weather, so an early start is useful. Small local food stops may be available during the trekking season, but availability should never be assumed. Carry your own basic snacks and sufficient drinking water. Nakthan to Rudranag Continue from Nakthan towards Rudranag Waterfall. Rudranag is one of the major landmarks on the Kheerganga trail. The waterfall and surrounding rocky landscape provide a natural place to pause, rest and enjoy the valley atmosphere. This section also marks the transition towards the more forested and uphill part of the trek. Rudranag to Kheerganga After Rudranag, the trail becomes more demanding as the gradient increases. The final section passes through forested terrain with pine and other Himalayan vegetation. Expect a steady uphill climb rather than a technical mountain ascent. Take regular short breaks instead of exhausting yourself early. As you climb higher, the forest gradually opens towards the Kheerganga meadow. Reach Kheerganga Reaching Kheerganga after several hours of walking is the reward. At the top, you can enjoy the surrounding Himalayan landscape and visit Parvati Kund, the natural hot water spring traditionally associated with Lord Shiva. The hot spring is one of the defining experiences of Kheerganga, although access and bathing arrangements can be subject to local administration and site rules. Important: Do not assume overnight camping is permitted at the summit. Current Forest Department restrictions prohibit overnight camping at Kheerganga. (The Tribune) CTA: Want to experience Kheerganga with a planned route and local support? → Contact Our Guide

itinerary.title: Return to Barshaini and Departure
itinerary.description: If you stay overnight in Barshaini, Kalga, Nakthan or Tosh, start the day according to your planned accommodation and transport schedule. For a standard Kheerganga visit, the summit itself should be treated as a day destination under the current regulations. If your itinerary allows, enjoy the morning views of the Parvati Valley before beginning the return journey. Kheerganga to Rudranag Retrace the forest trail carefully. Downhill walking can appear easier than the ascent, but steep and rocky sections can put significant pressure on your knees. Use trekking poles if needed and maintain a controlled pace. Rudranag to Nakthan Continue towards Rudranag and Nakthan. Take care on wet rocks, especially after rainfall. Mountain trails can become slippery very quickly. Nakthan to Barshaini From Nakthan, follow the established trail back towards Barshaini. Once you reach Barshaini, you can continue by road towards Kasol, Manikaran or Bhuntar, depending on your onward journey. CTA: Complete your Kheerganga adventure with us → Book This Trek Route Breakdown: Nakthan vs Kalga Trail There are two principal approaches commonly used between Barshaini and Kheerganga. Route 1: Barshaini – Nakthan – Rudranag – Kheerganga This is the classic and more commonly followed route. Route: Barshaini → Nakthan → Rudranag → Kheerganga Why choose the Nakthan route? * Popular and easier to follow * Passes through Nakthan Village * Scenic Parvati Valley views * Local food stops may be available in season * Rudranag Waterfall is directly on the route * Suitable for first-time trekkers when weather and trail conditions are favourable The Nakthan route is generally regarded as the more straightforward option for trekkers who want a clearly established trail. (Travel Coffee) Route 2: Barshaini – Kalga – Forest Trail – Kheerganga The Kalga approach offers a different trekking experience. Instead of following the Nakthan side, the trail passes through Kalga Village before entering denser forest terrain. Why choose the Kalga route? * More forest cover * Quieter atmosphere in many sections * Beautiful deodar and pine surroundings * Less exposed to direct sunlight * Excellent option for travellers who enjoy forest trails However, some sections can be less obvious than the main Nakthan route, especially when weather conditions are poor. For first-time trekkers travelling independently, local guidance is useful if trail conditions or visibility are uncertain. (Travel Coffee) Which route is better? For first-time trekkers: Nakthan route For forest scenery: Kalga route For a varied experience: Ascend by one route and return by the other, provided current trail conditions and local regulations allow it. Barshaini to Kheerganga Distance The commonly quoted Barshaini to Kheerganga distance is approximately 12 km one way. Depending on the exact route, trail diversions, local conditions and starting point, published distances can vary. Some route descriptions put the total closer to 12–14 km. (Travel Coffee) For planning purposes, trekkers should prepare for approximately 12 km of uphill walking from Barshaini. The round-trip walking distance can therefore approach 24 km, depending on the route taken. Kasol to Kheerganga Trek: Where Does It Actually Start? A common misconception is that the trek begins directly in Kasol. The Kasol to Kheerganga trek usually involves a road journey from Kasol to Barshaini, followed by the actual trek. Kasol to Barshaini is roughly 15–17 km by road, depending on the reference point and route. From Barshaini, the trekking trail begins. (NatureDiary) Typical Journey Kasol → Manikaran → Barshaini → Nakthan/Rudranag → Kheerganga This makes Barshaini the practical trekking base rather than Kasol itself. CTA: Planning your Kasol trip? Add Kheerganga to your itinerary → Book This Trek Kheerganga Hot Water Spring – Parvati Kund The Kheerganga hot water spring is the signature attraction of the trek. Known locally as Parvati Kund, the spring is associated with the religious traditions and legends of Lord Shiva and Parvati. After hiking through the valley and forests, reaching the warm natural water is a memorable part of the experience. However, visitors should follow the instructions provided by the local authorities at the site. Conditions around the spring, access arrangements and bathing facilities can change. Do not treat the spring as a swimming pool, and avoid using soaps, shampoos or other products in natural water. Essential Travel & Logistics Guide How to Reach Kheerganga From Delhi The most practical route is: Delhi → Chandigarh → Bhuntar → Kasol → Barshaini You can travel from Delhi towards Bhuntar by bus, taxi or other suitable transport options. From Bhuntar, continue towards Kasol and Manikaran through the Parvati Valley. From Kasol, continue by local transport or taxi towards Barshaini, the roadhead for Kheerganga. From Chandigarh The route is: Chandigarh → Bhuntar → Kasol → Manikaran → Barshaini Depending on road and traffic conditions, the journey can take considerably longer than the distance on a map suggests. Nearest Airport The nearest airport is Kullu-Manali Airport at Bhuntar. Himachal Pradesh's Forest Department identifies Bhuntar Airport as the nearest airport for the Kheerganga site. (HP Forest) From Kasol to Barshaini Barshaini is the last practical roadhead before beginning the Kheerganga trek. Arrange your return transport in advance during busy periods, particularly if you have a fixed bus, flight or train connection later in the day. Best Time to Visit Kheerganga The best time to visit Kheerganga is generally during the spring, summer and post-monsoon/autumn periods. March to June – Spring & Summer This is one of the most popular periods for the trek. Expect: * Pleasant daytime trekking temperatures * Green forests * Clearer mountain views during suitable weather * More visitors on the trail Carry a light jacket because temperatures can drop significantly at higher elevations. July to August – Monsoon Monsoon requires extra caution. Heavy rain can make: * Rocky sections slippery * Stream crossings more difficult * Forest trails muddy * Landslide-prone roads risky For inexperienced trekkers, this is not the ideal period. September to November – Autumn This is another excellent period for Kheerganga. The monsoon begins to retreat, trails can become more stable and the valley often offers clear mountain scenery. September to November is particularly attractive for trekkers who prefer cooler weather and fewer summer crowds. December to February – Winter Winter can bring snow and freezing temperatures at higher elevations. Trail conditions may change rapidly, and access can be affected by snowfall and weather. Always confirm current local conditions before travelling during winter. Kheerganga Trek Difficulty The Kheerganga Trek is generally classified as Easy to Moderate, but it should not be mistaken for a casual walk. The approximate 12 km ascent involves sustained uphill walking and an elevation gain of roughly 1,500–1,800 metres depending on the route and elevation reference used. (HP Forest) The final sections can feel demanding because of: * Continuous uphill gradient * Rocky terrain * Long trekking distance * Weather changes * Limited connectivity * Altitude A person with reasonable fitness can generally prepare for the trek with regular walking, stair climbing and basic cardio training. Packing Essentials for Kheerganga Trek Footwear Wear proper trekking shoes with: * Good grip * Ankle support * Comfortable fit * Water-resistant construction where possible Avoid starting the trek in smooth-soled casual shoes. Clothing Carry layered clothing: * Quick-dry T-shirts * Warm fleece * Light down/synthetic jacket * Trekking pants * Warm socks * Cap * Gloves during colder months Rain Protection Weather in the mountains can change quickly. Carry: * Rain jacket * Backpack rain cover * Waterproof pouches/dry bags Water & Food Carry sufficient drinking water and refill only where the source is considered safe. Pack energy-dense snacks such as: * Nuts * Energy bars * Dry fruits * Chocolate * ORS/electrolytes Other Essentials * Sunglasses * Sunscreen * Personal medicines * Basic first-aid kit * Power bank * Headlamp * Trekking poles * Identification documents * Sufficient cash Trail Rules & Eco-Tips Kheerganga is an ecologically sensitive Himalayan destination. Responsible trekking is essential. Follow a Zero-Litter Policy Carry every wrapper, bottle and piece of waste back with you. Do not leave plastic, food packaging or other waste along the trail. Carry Cash Do not depend on ATMs near the trek route. It is sensible to withdraw sufficient cash in Kasol or before entering the upper Parvati Valley. Mobile Connectivity Mobile connectivity becomes unreliable as you move deeper into the valley. Older and recent trekking guides consistently report weak or absent network connectivity on substantial portions of the trail, with occasional connectivity depending on operator and location. (Vargis Khan) Do not depend on mobile data for navigation or emergencies. Before leaving network coverage: 1. Inform someone about your route. 2. Share your expected return time. 3. Download offline maps. 4. Save important contact information. Respect Local Culture Kheerganga has strong religious significance. Dress respectfully around religious areas and follow instructions from local authorities and temple/site staff. Respect the Forest Do not: * Cut trees * Light unauthorized fires * Play loud music * Disturb wildlife * Use soap in natural water * Take shortcuts through sensitive areas Do You Need a Local Guide for Kheerganga? For the standard Nakthan–Rudranag route, an experienced trekker can often follow the established trail during good weather. However, a local guide is strongly recommended when: * You are a complete beginner * You are travelling during uncertain weather * Visibility is poor * You are taking the Kalga forest route * You are travelling with children or older members * You are unfamiliar with Himalayan terrain A local guide can also help with route decisions, local regulations and changing trail conditions. CTA: Need a local trekking expert? → Contact Our Guide Kheerganga Trek Safety Tips The mountains should always be treated with respect. Start Early An early start gives you more daylight and a better safety margin. This is especially important because current Kheerganga access rules require visitors to reach the area early and return within the permitted time window. faqs.question: 1. How many days are enough for a Jaisalmer trip?
faqs.answer: Three days and two nights is the minimum practical duration for Jaisalmer if you want to see the major attractions and experience the desert. For a more relaxed trip, 4 days / 3 nights is a better choice.

faqs.question: 2. What is the best time to visit Jaisalmer?
faqs.answer: October to March is generally the most comfortable period for sightseeing and desert activities. Winter is especially popular, although desert nights can be cold.

faqs.question: 3. How much does a Jaisalmer tour package cost?
faqs.answer: The cost depends on the hotel, number of nights, vehicle, desert camp, activities, meals and travel season. Current marketplace packages show a wide range, so travellers should compare inclusions rather than just the advertised starting price.

faqs.question: 4. Is a desert camp included in Jaisalmer tour packages?
faqs.answer: Many Jaisalmer packages include a desert camp, particularly itineraries designed around Sam Sand Dunes. However, the camp category, meals, camel safari and cultural programme vary by package and should be confirmed before booking.

faqs.question: 5. Is Jaisalmer good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. Jaisalmer works well for families when the itinerary balances sightseeing with rest. A 3–4 night package can combine the fort, havelis, Gadisar Lake and a comfortable desert experience.

faqs.question: 6. Can I combine Jaisalmer with Jodhpur?
faqs.answer: Yes. Jodhpur + Jaisalmer is one of the most popular Rajasthan combinations. Allow at least 4–5 days for a comfortable version of the trip.

faqs.question: 7. Can I customize my Jaisalmer tour package?
faqs.answer: Yes. A customized package can be designed around your travel dates, hotel category, vehicle, sightseeing preferences, desert activities, number of nights and additional Rajasthan destinations.

faqs.question: How cold does it get at high camps?
